exposure: time motion analysis of DDI sub-parameters
cohort: The study included 119 cases of umbilical cord prolapse managed at a single hospital over 12 years, excluding cord presentation, gestational age less than 26 weeks, and cases occurring outside the hospital.
finding: The study found no significant relation between the Decision-to-Delivery Interval (DDI) and maternal or neonatal outcomes in cord prolapse cases, suggesting rapid DDI can be achieved safely with good perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Rapid Decision-to-Delivery Intervals (DDI) for crash caesarean sections in umbilical cord prolapse were achieved, with no significant relationship found between DDI and maternal or neonatal outcomes.
